heading: Refraction
text:
### Refraction [IRET.11.3]

Refraction is a property of the activation, the flag [LDET.5.3] describes
([IRET.11]). Each terminal node also keeps a **refraction table** of the token
identities that fired in the engine's current **cycle generation**. The
generation advances on every working-memory assert and retract and once per
pump; an entry of an earlier generation is stale and matches nothing, so the
table empties without being walked. The table catches an activation formed
again for an identity that already fired before any change to working memory,
and so before the match could have ended ([IRET.11.3.2]). The token identity
is the activation's tuple of participating fact ids; the 32-bit token hash is a
pre-filter, **not** the key. An entry matches only when both its token hash
**and** its fact-id tuple match (`refract_identity_match`, `terminal.c`).

idris.name: iret_11_3__fact_ids
idris.note: The identity of a match is its tuple of participating fact ids, as the clause requires; the 32-bit hash pre-filter is an unobservable optimisation and is not modelled.

idris.name: iret_11_3__ids
idris.note: A token's identity: `map fid tfacts`.

idris.name: iret_11_3__now_ids
idris.note: The identities of the current match tuples -- what a kept token is looked up against.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tok_ids
idris.note: The identities of a table's tokens.

idris.name: ltac_5_4__same_tick_trace
idris.note: Two activations, two firings, each once. Executed.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_pairwise_short
idris.note: A distinct list whose members are pairwise equal has at most one.

idris.name: iret_7_7__consistent_distinct
idris.note: A consistent chain's activations carry distinct identities.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME. From the loaded network, after any inputs applied with no pump between them, a pump that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the pump begins: its activations are its distinct matches ([IRET.7.7], [IRET.11.1], in the view), each fires once and none twice ([IRET.11.3], [LDET.5.3], in the run), whatever the other rules emit and withdraw meanwhile. Rete/NetworkOnce.idr's theorem with the action-free frame replaced by this one; the plain network, so no cascade and no sweep. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the fixture: A's firings are its matches, 2. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_trace
idris.note: A fires once per match, twice, with B's RHS writing between: no identity fires twice. Executed.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_ttl
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE AND THE CLOCK. From the loaded clocked network, after any inputs -- data events and ticks that sweep -- prepared with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins, whatever the other rules emit and withdraw and whatever their endings cascade: a cascade's targets are emitted kinds, which a framed chain does not read. Rete/NetworkFrame.idr's theorem on the engine Rete/NetworkClocked.idr runs; a prepare that re-times is outside it and is Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr's. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE ENTITY FIXTURE: A's firings are its matches, 1, the replacement's; the replaced wrapper's is gone and the no-ops made none. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE ENTITY STATE: A fires for the replacement's match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent; the entity and the input relation, which no row targets, are left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: The theorem at the fixture: A's firings are its matches, 1. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_trace_ttl
idris.note: A fires once for its match, with B's RHS and its cascade inside the run: no identity fires twice. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE TICKED FIXTURE: A's firings are its matches after the sweep, 1; the expired fact's match is not among them. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE TICKED STATE: A fires for the surviving match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent, the kind-0 fact alone left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: The theorem at the two-fact fixture: A's firings are its matches, 2. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_run_ttl
idris.note: A fires once per match, twice, with B's RHS and its cascade between: no identity fires twice, and the id B withdrew is minted again for a new identity. Executed, firing by firing.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_clocked
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE, THE CLOCK AND THE RE-TIME. From the loaded clocked network, after any inputs -- data events, and ticks that sweep and re-time every timed chain -- prepared with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins: the matches the ticks made counted, the matches they ended not. Rete/NetworkFrameClocked.idr's theorem with Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's prepare. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__gated_is_an_instance` and `ltim_2_5_1__shut_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_trace
idris.note: A fires once, B fires once, no identity twice. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the opening fixture: A's firings are its matches, 1. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_trace
idris.note: A fires once for the match the tick made, with B's RHS and its cascade inside the run: no identity fires twice. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the shutting fixture: A's firings are its matches, 0. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_trace
idris.note: No identity remains to fire after the tick ended A's match. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the swept fixture: A's firings are its matches, 0. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_trace
idris.note: No identity remains after the sweep. Executed.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__unfired_all
idris.note: EVERY ACTIVATION UNFIRED, over every chain: what the agenda holds before any pump has run -- no identity has fired, so nothing is refracted.

idris.name: iret_11_3__all_of_nth
idris.note: A property of every indexed member is a property of every member.

idris.name: iret_11_3__applied_unfired
idris.note: And keep every activation unfired.

idris.name: iret_11_3__apply_unfired
idris.note: AN INPUT keeps every activation unfired: an assert by the lifecycle, a retraction of a live fact, a retraction of nothing.

idris.name: iret_11_3__assert_unfired
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps every activation unfired: a no-op changes nothing, an insert is of a fresh fact, a replace retracts a live fact then inserts a fresh one. The cases of Rete/NetworkDispatch.idr's `iret_19_1__assert_view`, each executed on the one-row rule below.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_same_set_length
idris.note: TWO DISTINCT LISTS WITH THE SAME MEMBERS HAVE ONE LENGTH: a terminal that holds each match once holds as many activations as there are matches.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop
idris.note: A token taken out of a list, by `==`.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop_distinct
idris.note: Taking a token out of a distinct list leaves a distinct list.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop_elem_fwd
idris.note: A member other than the one taken out is still there.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop_elem_inv
idris.note: What is left was there, and is not the one taken out.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop_length
idris.note: Taking out a member of a distinct list shortens it by one.

idris.name: iret_11_3__drop_none
idris.note: Taking out a token that is not there changes nothing.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_cons_neq
idris.note: A member of a list whose head tests unequal to it is in the tail.

idris.name: iret_11_3__fires_the_match_count
idris.note: THE COUNT: under the view, the activations of every chain are as many as its matches, so the pump's firings are the number of distinct matches, summed over the rules.

idris.name: iret_11_3__flags
idris.note: The `fired` flags of every chain's activations: the agenda before a pump, as flags.

idris.name: iret_11_3__insert_unfired
idris.note: INSERTING A FRESH FACT keeps every activation unfired: what it creates is unfired, what it keeps was. From Rete/NetworkTransferFlags.idr's `iret_19_1__insert_flags`.

idris.name: iret_11_3__match_count_from
idris.note: Chain by chain: a terminal that holds its recompute once holds as many activations as matches.

idris.name: iret_11_3__pump_fires_once_per_match
idris.note: THE THEOREM. For an action-free program, from the loaded network, after any inputs applied with no pump between them, a pump with fuel enough halts `Quiescent`, fires exactly as many times as there are activations, leaves every activation fired with its tuple, and every chain's tuples are exactly its recompute over working memory, none twice: once per match, and each match once. [IRET.7.7] and [IRET.11.1] in the view; [IRET.11.3] and [LDET.5.3] in the run. The clauses a duplicate firing breaks, held together.

idris.name: iret_11_3__pump_fires_once_per_match_from
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH, from any state where every activation is unfired and the view holds: a pump with fuel above the activation count halts `Quiescent`, fires exactly as many times as there are activations, and leaves every activation fired with its tuple; and every chain's tuples are exactly its recompute over working memory, none twice. The activations ARE the matches, each once, and each fires once. Under the frame: an action-free program (every rule only logs), inputs applied with no pump between them, fuel above the activation count.

idris.name: iret_11_3__retract_unfired
idris.note: RETRACTING A LIVE FACT keeps every activation unfired: a retraction creates nothing fired and keeps what survives as it was.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tok_eq_of
idris.note: Two equal tokens test equal.

idris.name: iret_19_2__retract_between_fires_once
idris.note: A RETRACTION BETWEEN ASSERTS, AND ONE OF NOTHING: two facts asserted, the first retracted by its id, then an id no fact carries. The survivor's activation fires once. Executed.

idris.name: iret_7_7__word_square_fires_once
idris.note: A DUPLICATE DOES NOT HAPPEN, rows first: three `Word` facts whose letters make each a row and the matching column, with a fourth that completes nothing, under a six-pattern self-join; the pump fires once, and the one chain holds the one match, `50 1 12 50 1 12` by key, each fact filling a row and its column. Executed. That the join tests transcribe the self-join's `where` clauses onto a letter table keyed by the fact's payload is checked by reading.

idris.name: iret_7_7__word_square_interleaved_fires_once
idris.note: AND INTERLEAVED, the issue's second pattern order (row, column, row, column, row, column): once, the one match with the columns beside their rows. Executed.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__entity_noop_fires_once
idris.note: AN ENTITY ASSERTED TWICE WITH ONE PAYLOAD is the no-op too: the Entity case with the payload equal. One firing. Executed.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_1__relation_noop_fires_once
idris.note: A RELATION ASSERTED TWICE is one fact and one activation: the second assert is the clause's no-op, `iret_11_3__assert_unfired`'s Relation case with the fact found. One firing. Executed.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__entity_replace_fires_once
idris.note: AND THE PUMP FIRES ONCE, on the fresh wrapper, id 1: the assert mints the fresh id against the memory the old wrapper is still in, so the replace does not reuse the hole its retraction leaves, and 'a fresh wrapper with a new `fact_id`' holds literally. Executed; a first draft said id 0 and the model said otherwise.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__replaced_is_unfired
idris.note: AN ENTITY ASSERTED TWICE WITH A CHANGED PAYLOAD is the clause's retract-and-replace: the first wrapper's activation ends and the fresh wrapper's is created unfired. Before the pump the one activation is unfired. Executed.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_5__load_unfired
idris.note: The loaded network, from the loader's alpha table: every activation unfired.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_5__load_unfired_from
idris.note: THE LOADED NETWORK holds unfired activations only: each root's seeding wave creates, and what it creates is unfired.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__ghost
idris.note: The refraction set of [IRET.11.3] beside the engine, kept through every operation and cleared where [IRET.11.3.2] clears it. A ghost: the engine never reads it, which is what the theorem shows it need not.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__refracted_fired
idris.note: Every identity in the set belongs to an activation carrying `fired`.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__refraction
idris.note: Every terminal's refraction set as one list of (ordinal, identity): the token identities that fired in the current cycle.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__sound
idris.note: THE SOUND GHOST: the view, and every identity in the set belonging to an activation carrying `fired` -- the set refuses nothing the flag does not.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_set_at
idris.note: A member of a list after an update at one position is an old member or the update of one.

idris.name: iret_11_3__engine_maybe
idris.note: The engine of a possible ghost; named so that no statement mentions a projection unapplied.

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: THE REFRACTION THEOREM, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network the ghost's engine is the history's engine, every refracted identity belongs to an activation carrying `fired`, and the selection of [IRET.11.4] 1a -- the first activation neither popped nor refracted -- is the model's first unfired activation. In the tick-free fragment the `fired` flag is the whole of refraction under each of the five statements of it, and Rete/FireLoop.idr's abstraction of refraction to that flag is grounded in the spec.

idris.name: iret_11_3__select_spec_agrees
idris.note: UNDER A SOUND GHOST the section's filtered selection is the model's: the set refuses nothing the flag does not.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_sampled
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH EVERY INPUT SAMPLED. From the loaded clocked network, after any steps -- each a sample with a data event or none -- consumed with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins. Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr's theorem through the expansion: a step is a tick then its event. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the sampled arrival: A's firings are its matches, 1. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_trace
idris.note: A fires once for the match the sampled arrival made, B's RHS and cascade inside the run: no identity fires twice. Executed.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__pairs_is_an_instance
idris.note: The sequence rule's firings are its matches, 2. Executed.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__trace
idris.note: Two identities, each fired once. Executed.

idris.name: iret_11_3__same_tuple_same_tok
idris.note: With distinct tuples, two tokens of one table with one tuple are one token.

idris.name: iret_11_3__same_tuple_same_act
idris.note: With distinct identities, two activations of one terminal with one match are one activation.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tuples_of
idris.note: The tuples of a table, in table order; named so that no statement mentions a projection unapplied.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tuples_of_append
idris.note: The tuples of an appended table are the appended tuples.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__distinct
idris.note: No two entries with the same identity, the property [IRET.11.3] keys on.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_append
idris.note: Disjoint distinct lists append to a distinct list.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_concat
idris.note: A distinct list of distinct, pairwise disjoint lists concatenates to a distinct list.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_filter
idris.note: A sublist by filter of a distinct list is distinct.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_map_filter
idris.note: A sublist by filter, under a map, stays distinct.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_map_inj
idris.note: An injective map keeps a list distinct.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_cons
idris.note: A member of a non-empty list is its head or a member of its tail. Once in NetworkRefraction and, as ldet_5_9__elem_cons, in NetworkOrderKeep; shared from here.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_tok_elem
idris.note: Membership of a token list, from the Bool to the proof.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_tok_false
idris.note: A Bool non-membership refutes membership.

idris.name: iret_11_3__elem_tok_true
idris.note: Membership of a token list, from the proof to the Bool.

idris.name: iret_11_3__not_elem_tok
idris.note: Refuted membership is Bool non-membership.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tok_eq
idris.note: Token identity: tuple equality is equality.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tok_eq_refl
idris.note: A tuple equals itself.

idris.name: iret_11_3__tok_neq
idris.note: Distinct tuples compare unequal.
